# AV1 start allocation unwind

**AI disclosure:** This file, including its title and all prose, was generated by AI.

Isolated candidate for [omarchy-m1-video#86](https://github.com/iconidentify/omarchy-m1-video/issues/86).
`avd_av1_start` leaked previously allocated `inst`/`pipe_state` when a later `avd_buf_alloc` failed, because the error path `kfree`d the context without `avd_av1_stop`. The #84 candidate already unwinds HEVC/H.264/VP9 that way; AV1 was untested.

This **does not claim AV1 hardware support**. Parent platform/release issue #8 stays open. No load/install.

## Run

```
python3 experiments/avd-av1-lifecycle/tests.py
```

Failure index 2 on the #84 candidate leaks one live allocation. The isolated `av1-unwind.patch` makes indices 1/2/3 leak-free. Replacing `avd_av1_stop(ctx)` with `kfree(av1_ctx)` fails the same oracle (exit 95). ASan/UBSan are enabled.


## Maintainer validation and boundaries

Nine test groups execute the exact extracted allocator/start/alloc_bufs/stop
functions, with the actual pinned avd_buf definition. Every buffer-failure index,
context allocation failure and successful start/stop is exercised. The framework
clears priv after stop; repeated stop is tested only with NULL priv, never a dangling
freed pointer. Reverting unwind detects the leak; removing the NULL guard triggers
a fatal UBSan error. Sanitizers cannot recover to a successful exit.

Codec context fields, DMA services, fifo size and the opaque CDF type remain
synthetic stand-ins, not a real kernel ABI or AV1 decode test. Temporary source/test
roots are cleaned after each suite. Optional AVD_SOURCE_CACHE is hash verified.

A full native ARM64 candidate module builds warning-free with -Werror against
existing matching 7.1.13-3-1-ARCH headers. See build-evidence.json for exact kernel,
base candidate, AV1 patch, source, header, compiler, log and module hashes. Nothing
was loaded or installed. Reproduce into a new directory:

    python3 experiments/avd-av1-lifecycle/build.py /tmp/av1-unwind-build --headers /path/to/matching/arm64/build

This extends the isolated #84 candidate; it does not edit either its original
patch/evidence or the shipped 15-patch stack. Later guarded qualification remains
on #87. Parent #8 and all AV1 hardware-support gates remain open.
